content.title: About
content.content: A meatless turnover (also known as a hot pocket) is a ready‑to‑heat baked pastry filled with a plant‑based mixture of soy protein, vegetables and spices. It is designed for quick preparation in a microwave or oven and is suitable for vegetarians.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turnovers were first introduced in the United States in the 1970s as a convenient snack for busy people.
The vegetarian version was developed in the early 2000s in response to growing demand for meat alternatives.
Flavor enhancers such as monosodium glutamate and natural spices are often used to mimic a meaty taste.
Each pocket typically contains about 200‑250 kcal, making it a suitable snack between meals.
The product is usually sold frozen, allowing long‑term storage without quality loss.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Soy protein in the filling provides a complete amino acid profile beneficial for muscle maintenance and metabolism.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with traditional meat hot pockets, the meatless version contains less saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain crust add fiber that aids normal digestion.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Soy protein and fortified ingredients supply vitamins B1, B2 and B6, important for energy production.

items.title: Cholesterol‑free
items.content: Absence of animal ingredients makes the product virtually free of cholesterol.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: The product contains soy protein, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salt is often added for flavor, so people monitoring sodium intake should limit portion size.

items.title: Possible trans fats in crust
items.content: Some crust formulations may include partially hydrogenated oils, which should be avoided on a low‑trans‑fat diet.

items.title: Requires thorough heating
items.content: Insufficiently heated portions may have cold spots, increasing the risk of food‑borne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Freeze‑thaw the pocket (or cook directly from frozen), heat in a microwave for 1.5‑2 minutes or in an oven at 180 °C for 12‑15 minutes. Serve hot, optionally with fresh veggies, a dip or a yogurt‑based sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, consume within 24 hours and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
